result.summary:
Re-ran the design gate from scratch on Revision 2 of lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md, read directly and in full (not from any prior summary). This time independently verified the mechanism claim against real Ecto.Multi source rather than trusting CODE-DESIGNER's or ELIXIR-DEV's assertions.

AC-by-AC / check-by-check verdicts:

1. Independent mechanism verification (own read of deps/ecto/lib/ecto/multi.ex, not just CODE-DESIGNER's citations) -- PASS. Read multi.ex:820-960 myself: __apply__/4 (:851-858) reverses multi.operations once, then apply_operations/5 (:875-881) runs a single Enum.reduce over that fixed-order list -- i.e. execution phase is one linear pass in composed order, no lookahead, no re-entry. apply_operation's :merge clause (:883-892) recursively applies a freshly-built nested Multi and folds results via merge_results/3 (:944-955), which raises immediately on any key already in the running `names` MapSet -- confirming the collision mechanism itself (§1) is accurately described. Grepped multi.ex for every public builder (run/3, merge/2, insert/3,4, delete/3,4, inspect/2 at lines 266-267, 280-282, 312-322, 438-448, 596-609, 845-847): every one calls `Map.update!(multi, :operations, &[... | &1])` -- pure prepend onto a list, zero pop/filter/replace primitive anywhere in the module. This directly confirms §2.1's central claim: there is no Ecto.Multi operation that removes or replaces an already-composed step, and by the time a later Multi.merge/2 callback runs (execution time), an earlier :run step for the same key has already executed. Build-time composition vs. execution-time evaluation is a real, load-bearing distinction in Ecto's own implementation, not an invented one. Separately verified §3.1's claim that find_waiting_parent_token/3 (the cascade ancestor lookup) is NOT build-time-visible: read sub_process.ex:1013-1052 directly -- it is invoked from inside Multi.run(cascade_lookup_key, fn repo, _changes -> find_waiting_parent_token(repo, ...) end), i.e. strictly execution-time (inside the reduce), confirming no plain-Elixir data exists before the outer Multi is built that could gate the cascade case the same way. Also cross-checked engine.ex:2572-2592 (build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3's current body) and engine.ex:2396-2467 (build_complete_task_tail_multi/6's second clause) against the design's own line citations -- both match current source (prepared_children destructured at the function head, parent_instance_id bound before call (1) at line 2412/2415, exactly as §2.2 states). The Revision 2 mechanism is mechanically sound: the predicate is evaluated in plain Elixir before either call (1) or call (2) is ever appended to any Multi, so it never needs to undo a step that has already run -- it only ever decides, once, whether to compose a step at all.

2. AC1/AC2/AC3 mapping in the revised document -- PASS. AC1 (no more raising on sync-completing child) maps to §2.2's predicate + §2.4's conditional gatekeeper at the build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 call site. AC2 (regression test scenario) maps to §5, carried forward unchanged from Revision 1 and confirmed still applicable since it tests observable behavior, not the internal mechanism. AC3 (async/queued path unchanged) maps to §4, re-derived under the new predicate and shown to reduce to today's unconditional behavior whenever no prepared_children entry is :completed.

3. No TBD/deferral language on anything an AC requires resolved -- PASS. Grepped the doc; no TBD/deferred hits on AC-required content. §6's two open questions (OQ-1: whether the predicate needs its own unit test; OQ-2: self-ancestor cascade reuse) are both test-coverage/scope judgment calls, not undetermined fix behavior -- see check 6 below for OQ-2 specifically.

4. No real .ex/.exs implementation code -- PASS. Grepped the doc for def/defp/function-body-shaped code blocks; only hit is a prose sentence at line 328 describing existing, unmodified code's behavior ('do: multi exactly as today'), not a new code block. The only fenced code block in the doc is the single @spec in §2.5.

5. Signature-change claim -- PASS, confirmed narrow as claimed. §2.5 states only build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3->4 changes (adds skip_task_activation?: boolean(), return type unchanged as bare Multi.t()), and explicitly withdraws all five of Revision 1's other signature changes (append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6, SubProcess.append_start_multi/7, maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6, append_completion_multi/5, build_completion_write_steps/12, maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6 all stated to keep their current, already-implemented arities). Cross-checked against actual current source: sub_process.ex:481 (maybe_chain_synchronous_completion), :1013 (maybe_cascade_to_grandparent) match the arities the design says are unchanged. No other signature is silently changed anywhere in the doc.

6. Cascade open question non-load-bearing -- PASS. §3.1-§3.2 and the design's own OQ-2 confirm the build-time predicate legitimately cannot extend to maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6 because the ancestor lookup (find_waiting_parent_token/3) only resolves at Multi-execution time (independently confirmed above, sub_process.ex:1013-1025) -- this is a real mechanical limit, not a convenience deferral. §1's own closing paragraph and §3.1 establish each ancestor level targets a distinct instance_id by construction in the normal case, so distinct Multi keys never collide regardless of build order -- no gate is needed for the reachable cascade case. The only unresolved gap is a self-ancestor-reuse edge case that ISS-0392's own filed scope and repro (docs/issues/ISS-0392.yaml, description) do not exercise -- confirmed by reading ISS-0392.yaml directly: the filed repro is explicitly a single-level SUB_PROCESS('sp') child completing synchronously against its own parent, not a multi-level self-referential cascade. This open question does not leave any AC's behavior for the actual bug being closed undetermined; it is honestly scoped as a possible follow-up issue, not silently resolved in either direction.

VERDICT: PASS. No gaps found; design is mechanically sound and ready for ELIXIR-DEV re-implementation.
